done_when: forge doctor --fix finds changed-by-hand files with one git status and one git log call for all of Forge's files instead of two calls per file, with the same results; a command test counts git calls per doctor --fix run and shows they no longer grow with the number of files; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each

findings.body: With `log.showRoot=false`, this invocation emits root commit metadata without its raw file records; I verified that behavior with read-only Git calls. Consequently, `entry()` treats files inherited unchanged from the root as absent. If a Forge file exists in the root, remains unchanged on the first parent, and is deleted by hand on a merged side branch, the merge's deletion incorrectly compares equal to the first parent's reconstructed state. `_history()` then returns no last change, allowing doctor to recreate the hand-deleted file instead of protecting it. Both default-branch repairs and in-place fix repairs use this helper. Add `--root` so reconstruction always receives the initial file contents, independently of the user's [Git configuration](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log#Documentation/git-log.txt-logshowRoot).
findings.title: Force root diffs when reconstructing merge-parent file contents

why: forge doctor --fix checks every Forge file with two git commands each (about 190 git processes per run)
